rect.title: Checksum Present (bit 0). If 1, the Checksum and Reserved1 fields are present and Checksum is valid — RFC 2784 §2.2
bit 1: drawn blank in RFC 2890 §2; inside Reserved0 (bits 1-12) per RFC 2784 §2.3; the Routing Present bit in RFC 1701
Key Present (bit 2). If 1, the Key field is present — RFC 2890 §2
Sequence Number Present (bit 3). If 1, the Sequence Number field is present — RFC 2890 §2
bits 4-12. A receiver MUST discard a packet with any of bits 1-5 non-zero unless it implements RFC 1701; bits 6-12 MUST be sent as zero and ignored on receipt
Version Number (bits 13-15) MUST be zero — RFC 2784 §2.3.1
EtherType of the payload packet (RFC 1700 / IANA ETHER TYPES); 0x0800 when the payload is IPv4
one's-complement checksum over the GRE header and the payload packet — RFC 2784 §2.5
MUST be transmitted as zero; present exactly when the Checksum field is present — RFC 2784 §2.6
four-octet flow identifier inserted by the encapsulator — RFC 2890 §2.1
four-octet counter for in-order delivery, starting at 0 — RFC 2890 §2.2

g.text: Present only if the C (Checksum Present) bit is 1 — RFC 2784 §2.2
Present only if the K (Key Present) bit is 1 — RFC 2890 §2
Present only if the S (Sequence Number Present) bit is 1 — RFC 2890 §2

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 bitfield # GRE header — transcribed from the ASCII diagram in RFC 2890 §2 # ("The proposed GRE header will have the following format", September 2000), # which is RFC 2784 §2.1's base header plus the K and S bits and the two # fields they gate. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2890.txt # # What this figure probes: fields whose PRESENCE depends on a flag bit # elsewhere in the same header — Checksum and Reserved1 iff C = 1, # Key iff K = 1, Sequence Number iff S = 1. # # Fidelity rule for this file: it carries EXACTLY the fields RFC 2890 §2 # draws. The payload packet follows on the wire (RFC 2784 §2 draws the # whole encapsulation) but is outside this diagram, so it is not a field. title "GRE header"
# Two carriers, two different jobs. # # present="C = 1" states THIS field's presence condition. It draws — a # caption under the block — so the human sees what the reading agent # sees. The VALUE is opaque prose: §12.7 lets an agent quote it and # forbids parsing it, evaluating it, or resolving `C` against the # `field "C"` declared below (the language has no reference grammar, # and a field name is a label, not an id — see `ANNOTATION-LOCATOR-SPLIT`). # # class=ifc states the CO-DEPENDENCY. Core §12.7 licenses a reading # agent to take a class reference plus that class's meaning as a # CATEGORY, so two fields carrying `class=ifc` are structurally in one # category and a reader may conclude they appear and disappear together. # That is real, machine-readable co-dependency, and it is the sanctioned # answer for a condition SHARED by several fields (genres/bitfield.md). # # Neither carrier resolves a name. Both are here because they say different # things, and the descriptions below no longer repeat the condition a third # time. class ifc "Present only if the C (Checksum Present) bit is 1 — RFC 2784 §2.2" class ifk "Present only if the K (Key Present) bit is 1 — RFC 2890 §2" class ifs "Present only if the S (Sequence Number Present) bit is 1 — RFC 2890 §2"
# msb0: bit 0 is the MSB, ruler 0…31 left to right, so the bit numbers the # RFC's own section headings use ("Checksum Present (bit 0)", "Reserved0 # (bits 1-12)", "Version Number (bits 13-15)") read straight off the ruler. bitfield gre "GRE Header (RFC 2890 §2)" word=32 numbering=msb0
# Word 0 — 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 3 + 16 = 32 bits. The four flag bits are # declared one per line so each gets its own bit position and its own note. field "C" 1 description="Checksum Present (bit 0). If 1, the Checksum and Reserved1 fields are present and Checksum is valid — RFC 2784 §2.2" # Bit 1 is drawn as an EMPTY cell in RFC 2890's figure and the RFC gives it # no name there, so this file gives it none either: `""` records an empty # label rather than inventing a caption. RFC 2784 §2.3 counts this bit # inside Reserved0 (bits 1-12); RFC 1701 used it as the Routing Present bit. field "" 1 description="bit 1: drawn blank in RFC 2890 §2; inside Reserved0 (bits 1-12) per RFC 2784 §2.3; the Routing Present bit in RFC 1701" field "K" 1 description="Key Present (bit 2). If 1, the Key field is present — RFC 2890 §2" field "S" 1 description="Sequence Number Present (bit 3). If 1, the Sequence Number field is present — RFC 2890 §2" field "Reserved0" 9 description="bits 4-12. A receiver MUST discard a packet with any of bits 1-5 non-zero unless it implements RFC 1701; bits 6-12 MUST be sent as zero and ignored on receipt" field "Ver" 3 description="Version Number (bits 13-15) MUST be zero — RFC 2784 §2.3.1" field "Protocol Type" 16 fill=#dbeafe description="EtherType of the payload packet (RFC 1700 / IANA ETHER TYPES); 0x0800 when the payload is IPv4"
# Word 1 — present as a pair, or not at all. `present=` is the language's # "present only if": the WIDTH is fixed and only the presence is not. A # reader computing offsets across a conditionally present field must branch # and emit both offset sets, one with it present and one without — the fields # below each move 32 bits earlier when C = 0. The renderer dashes the cell # and, because a condition is STATED here, draws it as a caption under the # block, so the human sees exactly what the reading agent sees. field "Checksum" 16 present="C = 1" class=ifc description="one's-complement checksum over the GRE header and the payload packet — RFC 2784 §2.5" field "Reserved1" 16 present="C = 1" class=ifc description="MUST be transmitted as zero; present exactly when the Checksum field is present — RFC 2784 §2.6"
# Word 2, then word 3. Independent of each other and of word 1: with C=0, # K=1, S=0 the Key is the SECOND word of the header, not the third. field "Key" 32 present="K = 1" class=ifk fill=#fef9c3 description="four-octet flow identifier inserted by the encapsulator — RFC 2890 §2.1" field "Sequence Number" 32 present="S = 1" class=ifs description="four-octet counter for in-order delivery, starting at 0 — RFC 2890 §2.2"
# Eight presence combinations (C, K, S independent) share this one drawing; # the diagram above is the all-present case, which is what RFC 2890 draws. # The header is 4 octets when C=K=S=0 and 16 octets when all three are set.
